proposals.text: Customers should obtain a shopping cart before doing the shopping trip, expressed by the possession-changing interaction rather than by a fixed cart-station coordinate.
Customers should not leave the store without their cart, a role-based exit norm independent of where the exit is located.
Customers must not take carts into single-file shelf aisles, identified geometrically by opposing shelves and very small horizontal clearance rather than by aisle coordinates.
Shelf interactions inside a single-file shelf aisle should be performed without a cart, which generalizes to any rotated or relocated narrow aisle described by local geometry.

If a customer leaves a cart behind, it should be parked in an open clear circulation area rather than beside shelves or inside a constricted aisle, using local clearance and shelf adjacency instead of fixed parking spots.
Parking a cart should be followed by a cart-free entry into a single-file shelf aisle, capturing the purpose of temporary parking without naming the aisle mouth location.
A customer who parks a cart should retrieve it before finishing the trip, a general unattended-cart norm tied to cart-possession transitions rather than to a particular recovery coordinate.

After coming back out of a single-file shelf aisle without a cart, the customer should recover the parked cart, generalizing to any aisle exit defined by the transition from constrained shelf geometry to open space.

{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.
